themes.consensus_view: Three banks flag Strait of Hormuz disruption as a live oil-and-shipping catalyst, with prediction markets pricing 61% odds of traffic returning to normal by end of July, but none have staked a directional view.

facts_agreed.claim: Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, and Morgan Stanley all flag Strait of Hormuz disruption as a current shipping and energy-flow concern.
evidence_quotes: Strait of Hormuz energy flow disruption

themes.consensus_view: Banks reference US-Iran deal negotiations as a live macro catalyst, but only JPMorgan stakes a view, pushing back on the simple deal-equals-lower-oil-and-inflation narrative as too clean.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple banks flag the US-Iran deal as an active negotiation thread shaping the near-term macro setup.

themes.consensus_view: Goldman expects the ECB to keep raising rates cautiously, with two quarter-point hikes pencilled in for June and September because tighter lending conditions are already slowing the economy.

facts_agreed.claim: Goldman forecasts 25 basis point ECB hikes in June and September, framing the path as cautious given tighter financial conditions.
evidence_quotes: consistent with our forecast for 25bp hikes in June and September
